articles.title: US tracked Alice Huang’s contacts with China spy agency during Nvidia affair
articles.summary: Washington: The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports that describe the encounters. The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Jensen Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips. US intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said. The extent and specific timing of Alice Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported. Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how US officials came to believe that Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation. Alice Huang left Megaspeed in 2025 amid a probe and ban from Singapore: More unravel amid Nvidia spy row They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Alice Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China. Allies of the former Nvidia chief, including President Donald Trump , have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Alice Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang. It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Alice Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s AI ambitions. US officials are investigating the role of Alice Huang and Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. US officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence. The intelligence gathered by the US contains evidence — including shipping records — demonstrating the role of Alice Huang and Kang in that network of companies, people with knowledge of the intelligence reports said. The New York Times has previously reported that Alice Huang and her family have a web of connections to Chinese defense contractors. Jensen Huang initially described his relationship with Alice Huang as normal interactions with a business customer. He acknowledged an affair only after the Times revealed last month that Alice Huang had been identified by the United States as a Chinese intelligence asset and that the Nvidia chief had been picked up on electronic surveillance targeting her. He stepped down this month after the Times subsequently reported that he had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia. Administration officials never provided him with a so-called defensive briefing about Alice Huang, a heads-up that the woman he was in a relationship with had been linked to Chinese intelligence. A spokesperson for Jensen Huang declined to comment. The White House, the State Department, the Chinese Embassy in Washington, Alice Huang and Kang did not respond to requests for comment on Sunday. Before the scandal broke into public view, advisers to Trump told him on at least two occasions that US intelligence had uncovered Alice Huang’s links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Jensen Huang while he was still running Nvidia, according to US officials with direct knowledge of the briefings. Both times, including when his national security adviser discussed it with him, the president downplayed the concerns and made clear he did not want to intervene in the matter. The officials said Trump regarded Jensen Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market. Trump has recently suggested that Nvidia should consider bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, a possibility the company’s board has rejected. “We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them,” the president said at a White House news conference on Friday. “I think the company if they were smart they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work.” Trump has claimed that no one in his government told him of any intelligence indicating that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset. “I don’t know that she is a spy,” he said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.” In fact, his administration has been monitoring Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency for more than a year, a period when the Ministry of State Security has been intensifying its new role in seeking to give China an advantage in artificial intelligence. “This network of companies working to procure and smuggle Nvidia chips lines up precisely with the MSS’s recently stated core mission of circumventing and undermining US export controls on semiconductors and other key technologies,” said Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first term, and who is CEO of the open-source research firm Garnaut Global. Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entry following investigation The Ministry of State Security has for decades declared that its mission is to combat espionage and to eliminate political threats to Communist Party rule in China. The minister of state security, Chen Yixin, gave a similar five-point statement as recently as late last year. Then in April, he unveiled a new, sixth mission — overcoming the “blockades” choking China’s access to key technologies like artificial intelligence. “Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development and applications,” Chen wrote in a party journal. “Focus on tackling the ‘choke holds’ of critical technologies.” “To assume the MSS wasn’t at the center of this operation would be to assume that they are incompetent,” Pottinger added. “That’s not an assumption I would make.” American spy agencies are still working to understand the role played by Kang, the business partner of Alice Huang, whom she would introduce to associates as her husband. Multiple people with knowledge of the intelligence said the United States had collected evidence that Kang worked with the Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang also appears to have met with officials of China’s Ministry of Public Security, the nation’s main law enforcement agency, according to multiple people with knowledge of the US intelligence reports. Alice Huang, Kang, Alice Huang’s sister and companies associated with them have emerged as a significant branch of the Chinese effort to build data centers and acquire access to Nvidia chips to train powerful AI models. Alice Huang’s network has been linked to efforts to supply the powerful chips to Chinese-state owned military contractors doing work for the People’s Liberation Army. Little of the intelligence about Alice Huang and her network has been provided to Capitol Hill, but lawmakers from both parties are demanding briefings. A briefing this month for top lawmakers by John Ratcliffe, the CIA director, and Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, was originally scheduled to discuss Iran, but the Times’ reporting on Nvidia led the lawmakers to ask questions about Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. Their answers raised more questions and left some lawmakers puzzled. Trump administration officials postponed a follow-up briefing for top national security staffers scheduled for last Wednesday, in which senior officials were set to share details of the intelligence collected on Alice Huang. The intelligence about Alice Huang was closely held inside the government until the Times reported the existence of the information in late October. Behind the scenes, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also the national security adviser, had written a confidential memo, dated March 30 this year, laying out Alice Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence.

DH Deciphers | History, faith and politics behind the Thiruparankundram Deepathoon dispute
articles.summary: Chennai: The Supreme Court on November 20 allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam on the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 24 as a one-time measure. However, the Tamil Nadu government has sought a review of the order. The government contended before the Supreme Court that the Karthigai Deepam is lit only at the Uchipillaiyar Temple, arguing that lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon — located very close to a dargah — might result in communal tensions. DH’s E T B Sivapriyan explains the controversy surrounding the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam, the significance of Thiruparankundram Hill, and the politics surrounding the temple. Where is Thiruparankundram, and what is the significance of Thiruparankundram Hill? Thiruparankundram, the first of the six abodes of Lord Murugan across Tamil Nadu, is located in Madurai, one of the oldest living cities in the world. Considered the Tamil god, Lord Murugan is one of the most worshipped deities in Tamil Nadu, transcending caste lines, particularly among backward communities. Thiruparankundram hill has been a haven of religious coexistence and communal harmony for centuries, hosting the Subramaniya Swamy Temple, Kasi Viswanathan Temple, and Sikandar Badusha dargah. People from the Hindu and Muslim communities in Thiruparankundram have lived together for centuries—members of both communities own shops outside the Murugan temple. The dargah is the most recent religious structure, dating back to the 17th century. Tamil Nadu moves Supreme Court seeking review of order allowing Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thiruparankundram hill Were there controversies in the past over the ownership of Thiruparankundram Hill? An ownership dispute arose about a century ago and was settled in 1923 by a Subordinate Judge of Madurai, who ruled that the whole hill, except “certain cultivated and assessed lands and the site of the mosque,” belonged to the Murugan Temple. Where is the Deepathoon located, and what is the current controversy? The Deepathoon (stone pillar) is located on Thiruparankundram Hill, very close to the Sikandar Badusha dargah, which Muslims across the state frequent. Right-wing organisations say the stone pillar is the place where the Deepam was traditionally lit on the day of the Karthigai Deepam festival and that the custom should be restored. However, the temple administration says there is no documented evidence of the Deepam being lit on the Deepathoon. The lamp for the Karthigai Deepam festival has been lit at the Uchipillaiyar Temple on the hill for the past 150 years, the temple says, and it wishes to maintain the custom. The state government also says the stone pillar could be a survey stone and has no religious significance. How did Thiruparankundram become a political battlefield? Photographs of people allegedly consuming meat on the hillock surfaced in early 2025, leading to strong objections from devotees of Lord Murugan. The photographs also led to a major confrontation between Ramanathapuram Lok Sabha MP K Nawaz Kani and then Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai, who accused the former of leading the group that consumed meat on the hill. Right-wing organisations in Tamil Nadu began raking up the issue of Thiruparankundram in February 2025 after a demand by a few Muslim organisations to rename the hillock as Sikandar Malai. During a protest against the demand on February 4, 2025, BJP leader H Raja attempted to stoke religious passions by calling Thiruparankundram the “Ayodhya of the South”. The BJP has also been trying to milk the issue to “rally Hindus” behind it, with even Prime Minister Narendra Modi visiting the temple earlier this year. The BJP’s TN manifesto for the 2026 elections promised that the lamp would be lit atop the hillock. A controversy also broke out as Hindu outfits objected to animal sacrifice by Muslims at the dargah. In October 2025, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court prohibited the ritual of animal sacrifice at the Sikandar dargah, with a third judge pronouncing the order after a two-judge Bench delivered a split verdict in June 2025. How did the issue land in court, and why did the then DMK government defy the High Court order? In December 2025, Rama Ravikumar, a known Hindu activist, moved the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court seeking an order to light the Karthigai Deepam atop Thiruparankundram hill instead of at the usual place. Justice G.R. Swaminathan ordered that the Deepam be lit at the Deepathoon, but HR&CE officials under the then DMK government lit the Deepam at the Uchipillaiyar Temple at 6 pm as per tradition. Supreme Court allows one-time Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thiruparankundram, stays Madras HC order As the petitioner, Rama Ravikumar, informed the court that the order had not been executed, Justice G.R. Swaminathan not only pulled up the DMK dispensation for breaching his order, but also asked CISF personnel guarding the High Court premises to accompany the petitioner and 10 others to the hill to help light the lamp. Fearing a law and order situation, the Madurai District Administration imposed prohibitory orders in Thiruparankundram until further orders. Eventually, the Deepam could not be lit at the Deepathoon, leading to contempt of court proceedings—in January 2026, a division bench of the Madras High Court upheld Justice Swaminathan’s order, and the issue landed in the Supreme Court. Why does the Tamil Nadu government want the centuries-old practice to continue, and what did it argue before the SC? The government believes lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, located close to the dargah, could lead to communal tensions. It believes that customs should not be changed and that lighting the Deepam at the Deepathoon instead of the Uchipillaiyar Temple might open a Pandora’s box. The state government feels such issues could trigger communal tensions in a state that has not witnessed any communal strife in many decades. What is the stand of the locals? Even as right-wing organisations and Muslim outfits fight it out, residents of Thiruparankundram have maintained that the controversy is unnecessary and that they have been co-existing peacefully for decades together. What did the Supreme Court say on November 20? The Supreme Court stayed the division bench order upholding the single judge’s directive on lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon. However, it said the Deepam can be lit this year at the Deepathoon with a limited number of people as a one-time measure. The Tamil Nadu government has now moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its order.

India's ties with Russia an 'added value', can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Netherlands sees India's continued engagement with Russia as an "added value," as it believes New Delhi can use its ties with Moscow to persuade it to end the Ukraine war, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said on Sunday. Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23. He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership. "We understand that India has its own history, its own role in the world and its own relations," Berendsen told PTI , responding to a question on India's strategic autonomy and its continued engagement with Moscow. India ready to extend 'any help' to end Russia-Ukraine war: EAM S Jaishankar "We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relation to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said. The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks from both sides. Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, while US-brokered peace talks have made little progress beyond a prisoner swap. Berendsen said India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, shared concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world. In his opening remarks at the meeting, Jaishankar said the two sides had elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership and were looking to expand cooperation in areas including semiconductors, technology, defence and renewable energy, while continuing their traditional collaboration in water, agriculture and health. "There are shared challenges. I think terrorism is one, climate change is another, where it's important we work together. So I'm really pleased today to have this chance to co-chair our inaugural dialogue mechanism for reviewing the strategic partnership," Jaishankar said. articles.summary: Doha: Skipper Tilak Varma's measured hundred and Abhishek Sharma's pitch-defying 70 remained the bright spots as India A succumbed to Pakistan A by 48 runs in a Group B match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament here on Sunday. Chasing 314 on a challenging surface was never going to be easy, but India remained hopeful as long as Abhishek, who hammered six fours and as many sixes during his 42-ball innings, was at the crease. Once he departed, the other Indian batters struggled to force the pace against Pakistan's bowlers, eventually finishing at 265 all out. Skipper Tilak (100, 149b) and Shahbaz Ahmed (56) added 112 runs for the seventh wicket, but India were always facing an uphill task as the asking rate frequently hovered above 10 runs an over. Until then, Abhishek had kept India afloat in the daunting chase with a glittering array of shots. The left-hander took particular liking to pacer Mohammad Imran, hitting him for two fours and two sixes before finding the boundary again in a sequence of five deliveries. His second six, over point, was a treat to watch. 'Deserve to celebrate': BCCI supports India U19 players' aggression following thrilling Asia Cup final win over Pakistan The assault helped Abhishek reach his half-century in just 31 balls, while his partner Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struggled to get going. After lifting Imran for a boundary through long-on, the young sensation tried to repeat the shot against the pacer, but this time a leading edge resulted in a simple catch for Abdul Samad in the deep. Pakistan skipper Samad soon introduced the spinners, but Abhishek continued his aggressive approach. He dispatched off-spinner Hasan Nawaz for two sixes and a four to keep India ticking. However, his entertaining knock came to an end when he mistimed a shot off Nawaz and was caught by Samad at mid-off. His dismissal sucked the momentum out of India's innings. Tilak, who struggled early in his stay, managing just eight runs off 36 balls, kept India going in the company of an aggressive Shahbaz. The second half of his innings was a little smoother, as he scored 42 runs off the next 59 balls, but the left-hander was still not at his fluent best. At the other end, Ahmed found his range from the outset, flicking Imran for a four and a six. But the standout shot was a swivel pull off pacer Ali Raza that sailed over fine leg for a six. Ahmed reached his half-century off 41 balls but fell at a crucial juncture. He tried to pull Raza but failed to generate sufficient power, falling to a catch by Nawaz in the deep. It left India tottering at 241 for eight, still a considerable distance away from the target of 314, and they were never able to make up that deficit. Earlier, middle-order batter Nawaz struck a breezy 79 to guide Pakistan A to a challenging 313 all out. Nawaz, a regular in Pakistan's senior white-ball teams, reached his half-century off 82 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes. Openers Maaz Sadaqat (59, 63b) and Shamyl Hussain (33, 23b) gave Pakistan a flying start, putting on 66 runs in just 7.5 overs. But Hussain lost his focus following a brief verbal altercation with Harshit Rana and was dismissed shortly afterwards, scooping a catch to Rana off Ayush Badoni. Rana soon returned to dismiss Rohail Nazir as Pakistan slipped to 67 for two. Prime Minister Modi, Sourav Ganguly, Virender Sehwag laud Indian team for gritty U19 Asia Cup title win over Pakistan From there, Nawaz took charge of Pakistan's innings. Nawaz and Sadaqat added 54 runs for the third wicket before Suryansh Shedge (2/55) ended the promising partnership by dismissing Sadaqat. Samad then added 65 runs with Nawaz for the fourth wicket as Pakistan maintained a scoring rate of over six runs an over. But Samad was run out after being caught short of his crease through a combined effort by Rinku Singh and wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra. India made a good comeback after Nawaz was dismissed by Shedge. Nawaz's powerful hit off the pacer was caught by Badoni near the deep-point boundary. Pakistan were 230 for five in 38.2 overs at that stage, before Farhan Yousaf struck 56 off 48 balls to take the team past the 300-run mark.

articles.title: PM Modi, Nepal PM Balendra Shah to meet on November 23; new air routes, economic aid on agenda
articles.summary: New Delhi: Kathmandu’s proposal for a $2-billion economic assistance package from New Delhi and its long-standing demand for additional routes for international flights entering Nepal through the airspace of India, including the vexed issue of making the L626 corridor bidirectional, are likely to figure in the talks between the prime ministers of the two countries on Monday. India may, in principle, agree to Nepal’s proposal for the economic assistance package but is likely to insist on phased disbursement linked to specific projects. The package is expected to include around $500 million as a grant for reconstruction and rehabilitation in areas devastated by the August 26 flash floods, which caused extensive damage along Nepal’s border with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. The remaining amount is likely to comprise a concessional loan of $1 billion and a $500 million grant for upgrading the Siddhartha Highway, connecting India to Pokhara in central Nepal. New Delhi may also agree on allowing more routes through its airspace for commercial passenger and cargo planes to fly in and out of Nepal but is likely to ask Kathmandu for reciprocal arrangement for aircraft using the airspace of Nepal to fly to and from the airport in Bagdogra in the northern region of West Bengal of India. Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in Delhi for first bilateral visit, to hold talks with PM Modi on Monday Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to host his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi for the first meeting between the two leaders. The meeting is likely to result in several agreements and announcements covering development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways and connectivity, besides expanding bilateral cooperation in climate change, disaster resilience, infrastructure and technology. A few hours after Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for his first visit to India after taking over as the prime minister of Nepal on March 27 this year, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called on him. “India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal,” Jaishankar posted on X after meeting Shah. Apart from meeting Modi, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu before his departure to Kathmandu on Monday. The two prime ministers are likely to discuss Kathmandu’s demand for New Delhi to allow three additional routes through the airspace of India for passenger and cargo aircraft to enter Nepal using Janakpur, Bhairahawa and Nepalgunj entry points. Nepal has been pressing India for improving viability of its new international airports at Pokhara and Bhairahawa, both constructed by state-owned companies of China. For Kathmandu, securing more air entry points through the airspace of India is crucial to shortening the circuitous flight paths that international carriers now must follow to reach Nepal. Most international flights at present enter Nepal at Simara in southcentral region of the country after flying through India, forcing the aircraft approaching from the west to take a significantly long detour. Nepal has been pressing for access through western entry points to cut flying time and fuel costs and improve the commercial prospects of the Bhairahawa and Pokhara international airports, which were inaugurated in 2022 and 2023, respectively. New Delhi has been concerned over China’s persistent bid to spread its geopolitical influence over Nepal and build strategic assets in the country, not only elbowing out but also posing a security threat to India. India-Nepal ties need a reset; Balendra Shah's visit could be the moment The two new airports were envisaged as Nepal’s second and third international gateways after Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. However, both have struggled to attract sustained international air traffic. While Pokhara has recently secured a scheduled Dubai service operated by Flydubai, Bhairahawa continues to remain without regular international passenger flights. The limited air connectivity has raised questions about the commercial viability of the two major infrastructure investments. Modi and Shah are also likely to discuss Nepal’s long-pending request to India to make the L626 air corridor bidirectional. The route through the airspace of India has been available to international flights leaving Nepal since November 19, 2009. India, however, has not been allowing aircraft to use it to enter Nepal. Kathmandu wants the restriction lifted to enable two-way traffic. But the two sides, according to diplomatic sources, have differences over the altitude at which inbound flights could use the corridor, with New Delhi proposing 39,000 feet against Kathmandu’s preference for around 29,000 feet. India has been cautious about giving its nod to Nepal’s request for the additional western routes through Bhairahawa and Nepalgunj, particularly because of their proximity to the Indian Air Force’s strategically important base in Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh. With the IAF using the base for fighter aircraft operations and exercises, India has been reluctant to permit civilian flights to fly at lower altitudes to enter Nepal through the three proposed new routes, citing the need to safeguard sensitive military installations and manage airspace used for defence operations. The discussions the two prime ministers on Monday are also expected to touch upon reciprocal access to airspace, with New Delhi seeking Kathmandu’s permission for civilian aircraft to use the airspace of Nepal while flying to and from Bagdogra airport in West Bengal in India. Kathmandu has indicated its willingness to consider New Delhi’s proposal, subject to technical study. New Delhi, however, may insist on a firm commitment from Kathmandu, sources told DH . Shah, an alumnus of Visvesvaraya Technological University in Karnataka , led the Rashtriya Swatantra Party to a landslide victory in parliamentary elections in Nepal in March, riding the wave of aspirations triggered by the Gen Z uprising, which had, in September 2025, swept Nepal and overthrown the government led by K P Sharma Oli of the Communist Party of Nepal (United Marxist-Leninist) or CPN-UML. Though Shah had used the ‘F’ word for both India and China in a late-night social media post in November 2025, New Delhi reached out to him, and Modi extended an invitation to him.
